desc:
Wix app integrations connect your app to payments, email, analytics, Wix business apps or your own server. Ecom Swift LLC builds each connection with secure key storage, retries and clear error messages, and tests it end to end.

## What are Wix app integrations?

Wix app integrations are the links between your app and the other services your users depend on. Examples include Stripe for payments, Mailchimp for email lists, Google Analytics for tracking, Wix Stores or Wix Bookings for business data, and a custom API on your own backend. An integration moves data in one or both directions and keeps both sides in step.

## Why integrations are worth doing carefully

Site owners rarely want another isolated tool. They want an app that fits into the tools they already run, so a new subscriber lands in their email list or a new order reaches their accounting system without retyping anything. An app that does this saves them time, and that is a strong reason to keep it installed.

The risk is that a weak integration fails quietly. An expired key, a changed API response or a service outage can drop data for days before anyone notices. The owner blames your app, not the outside service. That is why the work is as much about failure handling as about the happy path.

## How integrations change what your app can do

Each connection widens what your app can offer. A form widget that also writes to an email platform becomes a lead tool. A booking helper that reads from Wix Bookings becomes a scheduling assistant. A dashboard that shows data from your own backend becomes a control panel.

Good integrations also reduce support. When errors appear in the dashboard in plain words, owners can fix a bad key themselves. A sync log shows what moved and when. These details affect retention and support time, though outcomes vary by app and audience.

## What a solid integration includes

- Secrets stored in Wix Secrets Manager, never written into code or browser files.
- OAuth where the outside service supports it, and scoped keys where it does not.
- A defined sync for each data type, one direction or both.
- Webhook and event handling, so changes arrive without constant polling.
- Retries for failed calls, with sensible waiting between attempts.
- Handling for rate limits set by the outside service.
- Messages in the dashboard that name the problem and the next step.
- A field mapping screen when the two systems name things differently.
- A written guide to every connection, so your team can maintain it.

## How we build and test them

We begin by agreeing which data moves, in which direction and how often. Then we create the connection in your repository and test with sandbox accounts, so no real customer data is touched during development. We trigger failures on purpose, such as a wrong key or a service that does not respond, and check what the owner sees.

The Basic package connects one service for one data type. Standard connects several services, including data from a Wix business app, with webhooks, retries and a sync log. Premium adds scheduled sync, a mapping screen, rate limit handling and a handover call with a written guide. The outside services may have their own fees, which you pay to them directly.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Create sandbox or test accounts with each outside service.
- List the fields that must match between systems.
- Decide what should happen when a sync fails.
- Rotate keys if they were ever shared in plain text.

**Avoid:**
- Pasting API keys into chat or code comments.
- Passing along the whole record between apps when only a few fields matter.
- Ignoring failed calls and hoping they retry.
- Connecting to a production account before the sandbox test passes.

## Who this is for

An app owner whose users keep asking for a Mailchimp or Stripe link. A store tool that needs Wix Stores order data. A company with its own API that wants Wix site owners to use it.

## What we need from you

Documentation links for each service, sandbox credentials delivered through a safe channel, and collaborator access to your repository and Dev Center. We never need your Wix password. Tell us what a successful sync looks like, and we will build the tests around it.
